terminology.definition: Overall weighted credit-average score on a 10-point scale across all completed semesters.
Weighted credit-average grade achieved in a specific single academic semester.
Standard quantification of academic effort: typically 1 credit equals 1 lecture hour or 2 laboratory hours per week over a 15-week semester.
A mandatory foundational course that a student must pass before being permitted to enroll in an advanced course.
A credit course in which a student received an 'F' (Fail) or 'I' (Incomplete) grade that must be cleared via supplementary exams or re-registration.
Special academic dispensation allowing students with attendance between 65% and 74.9% to write exams upon approved medical or official representation grounds.
Disqualification from appearing in semester-end examinations due to attendance falling strictly below 65% or unresolved disciplinary suspension.
Official authenticated credential issued by the Examination Cell authorizing a student to enter the examination hall for semester-end assessments.
Numerical score from 0 (Fail) to 10 (Outstanding) assigned to letter grades (O=10, A+=9, A=8, B+=7, B=6, C=5, P=4, F=0).
Evaluation methodology wherein letter grades are mapped based on class mean and standard deviation rather than static raw percentage cutoffs.
Official certificate issued by the Registrar verifying that an individual is currently a bonafide, active, enrolled student of the university.
Official document releasing a student from university jurisdiction to pursue studies at another recognized institution.
An accelerated 7-week summer session allowing students to clear up to 2 backlog courses or accelerate degree completion.
A course chosen by a student outside their parent engineering discipline (e.g., an engineer taking a course in Economics or Philosophy).
Statutory disciplinary authority comprising senior faculty tasked with investigating code-of-conduct breaches, exam malpractice, and ragging incidents.

policies.title: Mandatory Attendance and Condonation Policy
policies.summary: Governs attendance requirements, minimum percentages, condonation limits, and detention criteria for all undergraduate and postgraduate students.
key_rules: Students must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in every registered theory and laboratory course.
Condonation between 65.0% and 74.9% may be granted strictly on valid medical grounds or approved university On-Duty representation.
Students with attendance below 65.0% are strictly detained ('W' or 'SA' grade) and not permitted to write Semester End Examinations (SEE).
Detained students must re-register for the course during subsequent regular semesters or the fast-track summer term.
Biometric / RFID classroom records must sync within 48 hours; manual corrections require HOD and Dean approval.
policies.applicable_audience: All registered undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral students.

policies.title: Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) Policy
policies.summary: Defines the structure, weightage, compensatory provisions, and moderation of continuous internal assessments.
key_rules: CIE accounts for 40% (or 50% depending on program regulation) of the total course assessment weightage.
Consists of two centralized written internal assessments (CIE 1 and CIE 2), quizzes, and course assignments.
A student must secure a minimum of 40% in aggregate CIE marks to be eligible to appear for the Semester End Examination (SEE).
A single compensatory assessment (re-test) is conducted only for students who missed CIE 1 or CIE 2 due to authenticated medical hospitalization or approved university representation.
Internal marks must be frozen and displayed to students at least 5 working days before the start of SEE.
policies.applicable_audience: All students and course instructors.

policies.title: Semester End Examination (SEE) and Evaluation Policy
policies.summary: Establishes procedural norms for semester-end written and practical assessments, passing criteria, and invigilation protocols.
key_rules: SEE accounts for 60% (or 50%) of the final course grade.
Minimum passing requirement is 35% in the SEE paper and 40% in aggregate (CIE + SEE).
Hall tickets are generated digitally via ExamShield only for students with no fee dues and attendance >= 75% (or approved condonation).
Entry to examination hall closes strictly 15 minutes after examination commencement.
Possession of mobile phones, smartwatches, or unauthorized paper inside examination halls constitutes Level-2 Malpractice.
policies.applicable_audience: All students, invigilators, and academic evaluators.

policies.title: Course Registration, Credit Limits, and Prerequisite Policy
policies.summary: Regulates semester enrollment, minimum and maximum credit thresholds, prerequisite enforcement, and audit course rules.
key_rules: Standard semester credit load is 20-24 credits for undergraduate programs.
A student with CGPA >= 8.0 may overload up to a maximum of 28 credits with HOD and Dean approval.
Students with backlogs and CGPA < 5.5 are restricted to a maximum underload of 16-18 credits.
Prerequisites cannot be bypassed; a student must achieve an evaluation grade in the prerequisite before enrolling in downstream courses.
Course registration must be completed on UniCampus ERP before the notified Date of Registration (DOR).
policies.applicable_audience: All enrolled students and Faculty Advisors.

policies.title: Course Add/Drop and Course Withdrawal Policy
policies.summary: Provides procedures and deadlines for students to adjust elective courses or withdraw from subjects without grade penalty.
key_rules: Add/drop window opens on Day 1 of classes and closes at 5:00 PM on the 10th working day of the semester.
Students can add or drop open electives and program electives, provided course section capacities permit.
Formal course withdrawal ('W' grade) is permitted up to the 8th week of the semester; 'W' grade does not impact CGPA calculation.
Dropped courses after the add/drop deadline do not entitle students to tuition fee refunds.
policies.applicable_audience: Undergraduate and postgraduate students.

policies.title: Backlog Arrears, Supplementary Exams, and Summer Term Policy
policies.summary: Establishes pathways for students with uncleared courses ('F' grade) to clear backlogs through supplementary exams and summer terms.
key_rules: Supplementary examinations are conducted immediately following the release of even-semester results for eligible courses.
Fast-track summer semester runs for 7 weeks; students may register for a maximum of 2 backlog courses.
Maximum allowable degree completion period is N + 2 years (6 years for 4-year B.Tech, 4 years for 2-year M.Tech/MBA).
Students who fail supplementary exams must re-register for the complete course during regular academic terms.
policies.applicable_audience: Students with active backlogs or grade improvement requests.

policies.title: Answer Script Viewing, Re-Totalling, and Re-Evaluation Policy
policies.summary: Outlines student rights and procedures to inspect evaluated exam scripts and contest grading anomalies.
key_rules: Students may apply for digital viewing of evaluated answer scripts within 7 days of result announcement on ExamShield.
Re-totalling (checking arithmetic summation) costs Rs. 300 per paper and is completed in 3 working days.
Formal re-evaluation costs Rs. 1,200 per paper; the script is blindly assessed by an independent senior evaluator.
If the marks change by >= 15%, the script is referred to a third evaluator; if marks increase by >= 10%, a 50% fee refund is issued.
The grade finalized after re-evaluation supersedes the earlier grade, even if the new mark is lower.
policies.applicable_audience: All students appearing in Semester End Examinations.

policies.title: University Scholarships and Financial Aid Policy
policies.summary: Details institutional merit scholarships, socio-economic need grants, sports endowments, and annual renewal criteria.
key_rules: Chancellor's Merit Scholarship awards 50% tuition waiver to top 2% students in each department with CGPA >= 9.0 and zero backlogs.
Merit-cum-Means Hardship Aid offers 25% to 50% tuition concession for students with family annual income < Rs. 4,50,000.
Scholarship renewals are audited annually in June; maintaining minimum CGPA >= 8.0 and zero disciplinary infractions is mandatory.
Scholarship credits are directly adjusted against semester tuition fees in PayVarsity; direct cash disbursements are prohibited.
policies.applicable_audience: Prospective and current enrolled students.

policies.title: Tuition, Hostel, and Incidental Fee Payment Policy
policies.summary: Defines semester fee deadlines, acceptable online payment methods, late payment penalty tiers, and financial holds.
key_rules: Semester tuition fees must be remitted within 15 calendar days from the date of billing announcement.
Late payment fine of Rs. 100 per day applies for the first 10 days; Rs. 250 per day thereafter up to 30 days.
Non-payment beyond 30 days results in an automated ERP financial hold, blocking course registration and exam hall tickets.
Two-part installment payment plans require prior written approval from the Chief Finance Officer before the billing deadline.
policies.applicable_audience: All enrolled students and parent guardians.

policies.title: Program Withdrawal and Tuition Fee Refund Policy
policies.summary: Regulates fee refunds upon program withdrawal, course cancellations, and caution deposit settlements in compliance with national statutory mandates.
key_rules: 100% refund (minus Rs. 1,000 processing fee) if formal withdrawal notice is received 15 days or more before the formal start of classes.
90% refund if received less than 15 days before class commencement.
80% refund if received within 15 days after classes commence.
50% refund if received between 16 and 30 days after classes commence; zero refund beyond 30 days.
Institutional Caution Deposit is 100% refundable upon graduation or withdrawal after comprehensive No-Dues clearance.
policies.applicable_audience: Admitted students withdrawing from university programs.

policies.title: Student Residential Housing and Hostel Allocation Policy
policies.summary: Establishes room allotment priorities, occupancy tiers, room maintenance obligations, and mess subscription rules.
key_rules: First-year outstation undergraduate students receive priority room allotment in Cauvery and Sarojini Halls.
Senior students select rooms through a merit-cum-preference lottery on DormTrack based on cumulative CGPA.
Room transfers during the academic semester are prohibited except on certified medical grounds backed by the Health Centre.
Subscription to the hostel dining mess is mandatory for all residential hostel occupants.
Subletting hostel beds or hosting unauthorized overnight guests incurs an immediate Rs. 5,000 fine and potential eviction.
policies.applicable_audience: All hostel resident students and residential wardens.

policies.title: Hostel Gate Pass, Curfew, and Overnight Leave Policy
policies.summary: Regulates student evening curfews, digital gate passes, out-of-station leaves, and parental SMS notifications.
key_rules: Night curfew: All resident students must swipe inside their designated hostel turnstiles by 9:30 PM (weekdays) / 10:30 PM (weekends).
Day out passes (up to 9:00 PM) are issued automatically via DormTrack digital QR credentials.
Overnight leaves (staying outside campus) require digital request on DormTrack at least 24 hours in advance with verified parent OTP consent.
Unreported absence during the 10:00 PM nightly roll call triggers an automated alert to parents and the Proctorial Board.
Repeated curfew violations (3 or more) lead to cancellation of hostel residency privileges.
policies.applicable_audience: Hostel residents and warden staff.

policies.title: Central Library Borrowing, Digital Resource, and Conduct Policy
policies.summary: Defines book borrowing quotas, loan periods, overdue fines, digital proxy access, and reference hall etiquette.
key_rules: Undergraduate students may borrow up to 4 books for 14 days; postgraduate students may borrow 6 books for 28 days.
Overdue fine is Rs. 5 per day per book for the first 7 days, increasing to Rs. 10 per day thereafter.
Reference collection items, rare journals, and course reserve copies cannot be removed from the library reading rooms.
Digital database proxy credentials (IEEE, ScienceDirect) are strictly personal; automated scraping or sharing accounts is prohibited.
Clearance of all library fines and book returns is mandatory for semester hall ticket release and graduation clearance.
policies.applicable_audience: All students, researchers, and faculty.

policies.title: Student Identity Card, Smart RFID Credential, and Access Policy
policies.summary: Mandates student identity badge display, RFID gate permissions, lost card protocols, and replacement charges.
key_rules: Students must visibly wear their official Demo University smart ID card at all times while inside campus premises.
The RFID card serves as access credential for campus turnstiles, library entry, hostel gates, and bus transport.
Lending or borrowing ID cards to facilitate proxy attendance or unauthorized gate entry is a disciplinary offense.
Loss of ID card must be reported immediately via ResolveDesk to deactivate RFID permissions in CampusPass.
Duplicate ID card costs Rs. 500 and is issued by the Security Office within 48 hours of fee payment.
policies.applicable_audience: All students, faculty, and administrative personnel.

policies.title: Bonafide Student Certificate and Document Verification Policy
policies.summary: Regulates the issuance of official study certificates, fee structure letters for bank loans, passport endorsements, and transit passes.
key_rules: Bonafide requests must be submitted online through the UniCampus ERP portal specifying the intended statutory purpose.
Standard bonafide certificates are generated digitally within 2 working days with an authenticated university QR code.
Specialized bonafide letters (such as bank loan fee schedules or visa sponsorship) require accounts verification and take 4 working days.
Students with active disciplinary suspension or total fee default cannot be issued bonafide certificates.
policies.applicable_audience: Enrolled students requiring official university documentation.

policies.title: Transfer Certificate (TC), Migration, and Institutional Discharge Policy
policies.summary: Governs the formal termination of student enrollment, issue of Transfer and Migration certificates, and permanent record archiving.
key_rules: Application for TC and Migration must be submitted via UniCampus ERP accompanied by comprehensive institutional No-Dues clearance.
TC indicates academic conduct, date of admission, date of leaving, and reason for departure.
Transfer certificates are dispatched within 7 working days following clearance of all academic, hostel, and financial liabilities.
A duplicate TC can only be issued upon submission of a police non-traceable certificate and an attested notary affidavit.
policies.applicable_audience: Graduating seniors and students withdrawing from the university.

policies.title: Student Internship and Corporate Training Regulations
policies.summary: Establishes eligibility criteria, approval workflows, credit transfer norms, and academic monitoring for off-campus internships.
key_rules: Summer internships (6-8 weeks) are permitted after completing the 4th semester for students with CGPA >= 6.0.
Semester-long internships (8th semester) are restricted to students with CGPA >= 7.0 and zero uncleared backlogs.
Students must obtain a formal No Objection Certificate (NOC) from CDC before joining any corporate internship.
Unapproved off-campus internships will not receive academic credit and absences will be marked unexcused.
policies.applicable_audience: Undergraduate and postgraduate students seeking industry training.

policies.title: On-Duty (OD) Leave and Co-Curricular Absence Policy
policies.summary: Governs excused absence approvals for sports representation, cultural fests, hackathons, and academic seminars.
key_rules: OD leave is limited to a maximum of 10 working days per semester across all courses.
OD applications must be submitted on ResolveDesk at least 3 days prior to the event, with formal event brochure attached.
Post-event OD claims require certificate of participation and must be submitted within 5 working days of return.
Approved OD days are factored into AttendEdge attendance calculations as 'Excused Present' for exam eligibility.
OD cannot be claimed for private personal travel or events not officially endorsed by the university.
policies.applicable_audience: Students participating in sports, technical competitions, and cultural events.

policies.title: Medical Leave and Health Absence Policy
policies.summary: Outlines reporting requirements, medical certificate endorsements, hospitalization verification, and psychiatric leave.
key_rules: Illness causing absence for 3 or more consecutive working days must be reported to the Health Centre and Faculty Advisor within 48 hours.
Medical certificates issued by private clinics must be presented in person to the Senior Medical Officer for verification within 3 days of resuming classes.
Prolonged medical illness exceeding 20 working days may warrant a formal semester break (leave of absence) without academic penalty.
False or fabricated medical certificates will be referred to the Disciplinary Committee, resulting in immediate semester suspension.
policies.applicable_audience: All students experiencing acute or chronic health conditions.

policies.title: Student Grievance Redressal and Ombudsman Policy
policies.summary: Establishes formal channels for students to resolve academic disputes, unfair grading allegations, administrative delays, and harassment.
key_rules: Level 1: Grievance logged on ResolveDesk is assigned to the respective Department Grievance Cell (SLA: 5 working days).
Level 2: Unresolved tickets escalate to the Central Student Grievance Redressal Committee chaired by Dean of Student Welfare (SLA: 10 days).
Level 3: Final appeal lies with the Independent University Student Ombudsman appointed by the Board of Management.
Retaliation or discrimination against a student for filing a bona fide grievance is strictly prohibited.
policies.applicable_audience: All enrolled students and student groups.

policies.title: Zero-Tolerance Anti-Ragging and Harassment Policy
policies.summary: Enforces strict statutory zero-tolerance measures against ragging, bullying, intimidation, and unauthorized hazing rituals.
key_rules: Ragging in any form—verbal, physical, psychological, online, or in residential spaces—is strictly prohibited.
All admitted students and parents must submit an annual digital anti-ragging affidavit during registration.
Any student found guilty by the Anti-Ragging Committee faces immediate suspension, hostel expulsion, and police FIR filing.
Anonymous reports can be submitted via the 24x7 Anti-Ragging Emergency Hotline (phone / ResolveDesk anonymous portal).
policies.applicable_audience: Entire university campus community.

policies.title: Student Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedures
policies.summary: Regulates on-campus behavioral standards, substance prohibitions, property safety, and Proctorial Board inquiry protocols.
key_rules: Possession or consumption of alcohol, tobacco, narcotics, or dangerous contraband on campus results in immediate expulsion.
Willful damage to university laboratory equipment, computing systems, or estate structures requires full financial restitution plus fine.
Physical altercation or assault warrants instant interim suspension pending formal Proctorial Board inquiry.
Students charged before the Disciplinary Board are entitled to a fair hearing and may present written evidence.
policies.applicable_audience: All students, student clubs, and campus organizations.

policies.title: Campus Recruitment and Placement Eligibility Policy
policies.summary: Sets academic criteria, drive registration protocols, offer acceptance rules, and conduct standards for campus placements.
key_rules: Students must maintain minimum 60% (or 6.5 CGPA) throughout all semesters with zero active backlogs to register on CareerHub.
Attendance in training workshops and mock interview sessions conducted by CPTD must be >= 85%.
Strict 'One-Student-One-Job' policy: Once a student receives an offer with CTC < Rs. 8 LPA, they are eligible only for Dream companies (> Rs. 12 LPA).
Unexcused absence from an interview after registering for a company drive results in automatic debarment from the next 3 placement drives.
policies.applicable_audience: Pre-final and final year undergraduate and postgraduate students.

policies.title: Degree Award and Graduation Requirements Policy
policies.summary: Defines statutory criteria required to qualify for the conferment of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral degrees.
key_rules: Earn the minimum prescribed credits: 160 credits for 4-year B.Tech, 84 credits for 2-year MBA, 72 credits for 2-year M.Tech.
Attain a minimum cumulative CGPA of 5.00 for undergraduate degrees and 6.00 for postgraduate degrees.
Achieve a pass grade in all mandatory non-credit courses (Environmental Studies, Professional Ethics, Physical Education/NSS).
Zero uncleared backlog courses and zero active disciplinary proceedings.
Obtain complete institutional No-Dues clearance from Library, Hostels, Departments, Labs, and Accounts.
policies.applicable_audience: All graduating students.

policies.title: Student Clubs, Societies, and Activity Sanction Policy
policies.summary: Regulates the establishment of student interest clubs, event budget sanctions, social media guidelines, and faculty mentorship.
key_rules: Every student club must have at least 20 active members and an approved full-time faculty mentor.
Club events and guest lectures must be formally sanctioned on ResolveDesk at least 10 working days in advance.
Collecting unauthorized membership fees or off-campus corporate sponsorships without Finance Office approval is prohibited.
All official public announcements and social media handles must adhere to Demo University brand identity guidelines.
policies.applicable_audience: Student clubs, societies, and event organizers.

processes.title: Attendance Shortage Condonation Application Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student checks shortage alert on AttendEdge and collects original medical certificate / approved OD sanction letters.
Step 2: Student submits medical records to Campus Health Centre for physician verification and seal.
Step 3: Student logs a Condonation Request ticket on ResolveDesk, attaching verified medical proof and coursewise attendance sheets.
Step 4: Respective Course Instructors and HOD endorse the attendance mitigation in UniCampus ERP.
Step 5: Dean of Academic Affairs reviews appeal; if approved, ERP waives the examination detention flag.
Step 6: ExamShield generates the student's exam hall ticket.

processes.title: Compensatory CIE Assessment (Re-test) Scheduling Workflow
processes.initiator: Student (missed CIE 1 or 2 due to medical/OD)
processes.sla: Application within 3 days of missed test
steps: Step 1: Student submits formal compensatory exam application form on ResolveDesk with supporting medical/OD proof.
Step 2: Department Program Coordinator verifies genuine nature of absence and checks re-test eligibility.
Step 3: HOD approves request and instructs course coordinator to formulate compensatory test question paper.
Step 4: Department notifies date and classroom for centralized compensatory assessment.
Step 5: Evaluated marks are uploaded directly to ExamShield portal replacing the absent score.

processes.title: Semester End Examination Hall Ticket Generation Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student clears outstanding tuition and hostel fee arrears on PayVarsity.
Step 2: Course instructors finalize and freeze attendance and CIE marks on AttendEdge.
Step 3: ExamShield runs automated eligibility audit checking fee clearance, attendance >= 75%, and CIE >= 40%.
Step 4: Eligible students log in to ExamShield, download digital hall ticket containing barcode and assigned seating.
Step 5: Ineligible students receive automated detention notice specifying reason (Fee Hold / Attendance Detention / CIE Shortage).

processes.title: Semester Course Registration and Enrollment Workflow
processes.sla: Completed during notified DOR window (5 working days)
steps: Step 1: Student logs in to UniCampus ERP using student credentials.
Step 2: System displays core mandatory courses and available program/open electives based on prerequisite clearance.
Step 3: Student selects desired elective courses and submits provisional registration basket.
Step 4: Assigned Faculty Advisor reviews student course basket and verifies credit limits (20-24 credits).
Step 5: Faculty Advisor digitally approves enrollment; course rosters are populated in LearnSphere LMS.

processes.title: Elective Course Add/Drop and Section Change Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student navigates to Add/Drop Module on UniCampus ERP.
Step 2: Selects registered elective to drop and chooses replacement elective from courses with vacant seats.
Step 3: System checks that prerequisite requirements and maximum credit load rules are not violated.
Step 4: Faculty Advisor approves request digitally.
Step 5: Student LearnSphere LMS course access and AttendEdge biometric rosters are updated automatically overnight.

processes.title: Supplementary / Backlog Examination Registration Workflow
processes.sla: Within 10 days of regular result declaration
steps: Step 1: Student logs in to ExamShield and reviews list of eligible backlog subjects.
Step 2: Selects backlog subjects to attempt in the upcoming supplementary examination.
Step 3: System redirects to PayVarsity gateway to pay backlog examination fee (Rs. 600 per paper).
Step 4: Transaction confirmation generates supplementary exam registration receipt.
Step 5: Examination Cell allots exam date and issues supplementary hall ticket 3 days prior to exam.

processes.title: Examination Script Viewing and Re-evaluation Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student applies for answer script digital copy on ExamShield within 7 days of results (Fee: Rs. 400).
Step 2: Examination Cell uploads scanned copy of evaluated answer book to student portal.
Step 3: Student consults course instructor; if grading discrepancy is identified, submits formal Re-evaluation Request (Fee: Rs. 1,200).
Step 4: Examination Cell masks original evaluator markings and dispatches script to an independent external evaluator.
Step 5: If revised marks differ by >= 15%, third evaluator arbitrates; updated marks are published on ExamShield and ERP.

processes.title: Annual Merit Scholarship Renewal and Verification Workflow
steps: Step 1: Office of Student Welfare pulls cumulative academic performance and discipline records from ERP.
Step 2: Checks candidate against renewal criteria: CGPA >= 8.0, zero active backlogs, zero disciplinary sanctions.
Step 3: Approved renewal roster is signed by Dean of Student Welfare and transmitted to Finance Office.
Step 4: Finance Office posts 50% tuition waiver credit directly to student PayVarsity semester fee ledger.
Step 5: Student receives automated confirmation email and updated fee invoice for remaining dues.

processes.title: Semester Tuition Fee Payment and Receipt Generation Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student logs in to PayVarsity portal and views current semester fee demand statement.
Step 2: Selects payment method (UPI, Net Banking, Credit Card, or NEFT/RTGS Challan).
Step 3: Authorizes payment through secure banking gateway.
Step 4: Gateway transmits success response to PayVarsity; ERP updates student ledger balance to zero.
Step 5: Student downloads digitally signed, GST-compliant tuition fee receipt; financial holds are removed instantly.

processes.title: Formal Program Withdrawal and Caution Deposit Refund Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student submits formal withdrawal application on ResolveDesk with parental signature and bank details.
Step 2: Student completes online No-Dues clearance across Library, Hostels, Labs, and Department.
Step 3: Admissions Office cancels student enrollment in UniCampus ERP and archives records.
Step 4: Finance Office calculates statutory refund percentage based on date of withdrawal application.
Step 5: Approved refund and caution deposit are credited to student's verified bank account via NEFT.

processes.title: Hostel Room Allotment and Check-In Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student submits room preference (Single, Twin, or 4-sharing) and mess plan on DormTrack.
Step 2: System computes allocation based on reservation criteria (first-years) or CGPA merit (seniors).
Step 3: Student pays hostel accommodation and mess fees on PayVarsity within 48 hours to confirm slot.
Step 4: Student arrives at designated hostel on check-in day; caretaker inspects room inventory and hands over keys.
Step 5: Caretaker activates student RFID card on hostel biometric turnstiles in CampusPass.

processes.title: Hostel Night Out and Weekend Leave Approval Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student logs in to DormTrack and creates 'Out of Station / Night Out' leave request with travel destination and dates.
Step 2: DormTrack dispatches an automated SMS with 6-digit OTP verification to registered parent/guardian mobile.
Step 3: Parent provides OTP to confirm consent.
Step 4: Residential Warden reviews and grants digital approval; a dynamic QR gate pass is generated on student mobile app.
Step 5: Student scans QR pass at campus main gate turnstile; exit timestamp is logged in CampusPass.

processes.title: Library Book Checkout, Renewal, and Fine Settlement Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student selects book from library stacks and approaches RFID self-checkout kiosk or circulation counter.
Step 2: Scans student RFID ID card and places books on reader pad.
Step 3: LibNet checks account status (zero overdue fines > Rs. 50 and borrowing quota available).
Step 4: System issues book for 14 days and prints due date receipt; book RFID security tag is demagnetized.
Step 5: To renew, student accesses LibNet online before the due date, provided no other user has placed a reservation hold.

processes.title: Lost RFID Student ID Card Replacement Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student logs into ResolveDesk and registers a 'Lost ID Card' incident; CampusPass deactivates old RFID tag immediately.
Step 2: Student pays duplicate ID fee of Rs. 500 on PayVarsity and saves digital receipt.
Step 3: Visits Central Security Office (Main Gate) and presents fee receipt along with government photo ID.
Step 4: Security staff prints new RFID smart card with updated chip serial number.
Step 5: IT system updates CampusPass, syncs card with LibNet library database and hostel turnstiles.

processes.title: Online Bonafide Certificate Application and Generation Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student navigates to Student Services > Certificates on UniCampus ERP.
Step 2: Selects certificate type (General Study Proof / Education Loan Fee Structure / Passport Verification / Bus Pass).
Step 3: Enters applicant details, statutory authority name, and uploads supporting requirement letter if requested.
Step 4: ERP verifies active enrollment status and checks for disciplinary locks.
Step 5: Digitally signed bonafide certificate with verifiable QR verification link is generated as downloadable PDF.

processes.title: Transfer and Migration Certificate Issuance Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student initiates institutional No-Dues clearance request on UniCampus ERP.
Step 2: Department Labs, Library, Hostels, Sports Centre, and Finance Office grant clearance sign-offs.
Step 3: Admissions Office reviews completed clearance and prepares Transfer Certificate (TC) and Migration Certificate.
Step 4: University Registrar formally signs and affixes official embossed seal.
Step 5: Hard copy certificates are issued in person at Registrar counter or dispatched via registered speed post.

processes.title: Corporate Internship No Objection Certificate (NOC) Workflow
steps: Step 1: Student uploads official company offer letter with internship dates, stipend, and job responsibilities on CareerHub.
Step 2: Placement Officer verifies employer credentials and validates academic eligibility criteria.
Step 3: Department HOD and Faculty Advisor review potential clash with academic coursework.
Step 4: If approved, CDC generates digitally authenticated institutional No Objection Certificate (NOC).
Step 5: Student submits copy of signed NOC to employer and uploads confirmation to ERP.

processes.title: On-Duty (OD) Leave Approval and Attendance Adjustment Workflow
processes.sla: Apply 3 days before; claim verified within 5 days post-event
steps: Step 1: Student creates OD application ticket on ResolveDesk attaching official event invitation / sports fixture.
Step 2: Faculty Coordinator (Sports Director / Club Mentor) endorses university representation.
Step 3: Dean of Student Affairs (DSA) grants administrative approval.
Step 4: Following event completion, student uploads participation certificate and event report.
Step 5: AttendEdge automatically adjusts class attendance for the approved dates to 'Excused OD'.

processes.title: Medical Illness Verification and Attendance Endorsement Workflow
processes.initiator: Student recovering from serious medical condition
processes.sla: Within 3 working days of returning to campus
steps: Step 1: Student visits Campus Health Centre carrying hospital discharge summary, medical prescriptions, and lab diagnostic reports.
Step 2: Senior Medical Officer examines patient, reviews clinical documents, and validates illness duration.
Step 3: Medical Officer issues an official University Medical Verification Slip with unique endorsement code.
Step 4: Student uploads medical slip to ResolveDesk under 'Medical Leave Submission'.
Step 5: Faculty Advisor and HOD review slip and forward endorsed recommendation to Academic Affairs for condonation.

processes.title: Formal Student Grievance Lodging and Escalation Workflow
processes.sla: Level 1: 5 days; Level 2: 10 days; Level 3: 20 days
steps: Step 1: Student logs into ResolveDesk and submits formal grievance under specific category (Academic / Hostel / Finance / Harassment).
Step 2: Ticket is routed to Level 1 Department Grievance Officer; officer investigates and posts resolution within 5 working days.
Step 3: If student is dissatisfied, clicks 'Escalate to Level 2' within 48 hours; ticket moves to Central Grievance Redressal Committee.
Step 4: Committee convenes hearing with student and concerned department within 10 working days.
Step 5: If unresolved, matter is referred to the University Ombudsman for independent final determination.

processes.title: Anti-Ragging Incident Investigation and Emergency Action Workflow
steps: Step 1: Complaint is received via emergency phone helpline, ResolveDesk anonymous drop, or in person.
Step 2: Anti-Ragging Flying Squad mobilizes immediately; victim is relocated to secure accommodation.
Step 3: Dean of Student Welfare convenes emergency hearing of Anti-Ragging Committee within 24 hours.
Step 4: Committee questions witnesses, reviews CCTV and digital evidence, and formulates investigative report.
Step 5: If substantiated, Vice-Chancellor ratifies immediate expulsion, hostel eviction, and transmission of FIR to police.

processes.title: Proctorial Board Disciplinary Inquiry Workflow
processes.initiator: Security / Faculty / Hostel Warden reporting infraction
steps: Step 1: Reporting authority submits formal incident report and evidence to Office of Student Welfare.
Step 2: Proctorial Board issues show-cause notice to student detailing allegations and hearing schedule.
Step 3: Student appears before Proctorial Board, reviews evidence, and submits written defense.
Step 4: Board deliberates in camera and decides penalty (Admonition / Community Service / Fine / Suspension / Expulsion).
Step 5: Registrar issues formal disciplinary order; penalty is recorded in student ERP file.

processes.title: On-Campus Company Recruitment Drive Participation Workflow
steps: Step 1: CDC publishes company job notification on CareerHub specifying CTC, job role, and eligibility criteria.
Step 2: Eligible students register for company drive before notified registration deadline.
Step 3: CDC schedules online coding assessment in Central Computing Centre / online testing portal.
Step 4: Shortlisted candidates attend technical and HR interview rounds in Ramanujan Block.
Step 5: Company releases select list; placed students sign digital offer acceptance on CareerHub.

processes.title: Pre-Final Year Internship Eligibility Verification Workflow
steps: Step 1: CareerHub pulls student CGPA and backlog status from UniCampus ERP.
Step 2: System verifies student meets minimum threshold (CGPA >= 6.0 and zero backlogs for on-campus drives).
Step 3: Student completes mandatory resume upload and attends CPTD orientation session.
Step 4: CDC approves student profile for upcoming summer internship drives.
Step 5: Ineligible students receive specific deficiency report with remediation steps.

processes.title: Final Degree Graduation Audit and Convocation Registration Workflow
steps: Step 1: UniCampus ERP automated graduation audit engine evaluates total earned credits against curriculum requirements (160 credits).
Step 2: System checks mandatory non-credit course completions and validates cumulative CGPA >= 5.00.
Step 3: Academic Affairs verifies degree eligibility and publishes Provisional Graduands List.
Step 4: Graduating students submit convocation attendance registration and robe size preferences on ERP.
Step 5: Board of Management approves degree conferment; diplomas are presented at annual convocation ceremony.

processes.title: Student Club Event Sanction and Venue Allotment Workflow
processes.sla: Submit 10 working days prior to event
steps: Step 1: Club executive committee drafts event proposal containing budget, schedule, guest speakers, and venue requirements.
Step 2: Faculty Club Mentor reviews and signs off on proposal.
Step 3: Club submits Event Sanction application on ResolveDesk to Clubs and Student Activities Council (SAC).
Step 4: SAC coordinates with Campus Operations for auditorium allocation and Security for visitor gate access.
Step 5: SAC Chair issues official sanction letter; event is listed on campus activity calendar.

roles.title: Vice-Chancellor
roles.description: Principal academic and executive officer presiding over university academic council, senate, and administrative faculties.

roles.title: Registrar
roles.description: Custodian of university records, common seal, statutory affiliations, legal contracts, and official institutional correspondence.

roles.title: Dean of Academic Affairs
roles.description: Administers curricula, autonomous academic regulations, course registration frameworks, and degree audit policies.

roles.title: Controller of Examinations
roles.description: Heads the confidential examination cell, oversees question paper setting, evaluation integrity, result tabulations, and convocation lists.

roles.title: Dean of Student Affairs
roles.description: Guides non-academic student life, approves official On-Duty (OD) permissions, mentors student leadership bodies, and coordinates campus events.

roles.title: Dean of Student Welfare
roles.description: Safeguards student rights, presides over the Proctorial Disciplinary Board, oversees mental wellness counseling, and directs anti-ragging vigilance.

roles.title: Dean of Research and Innovation
roles.description: Facilitates sponsored research grants, supervises doctoral Ph.D. registrations and reviews, and oversees university patent filings.

roles.title: Chief Finance Officer / Bursar
roles.description: Manages university financial budgets, fee collection schedules, scholarship disbursements, institutional payroll, and annual fiscal audits.

roles.title: Head of Department (HOD)
roles.description: Leads faculty, manages department curriculum execution, laboratory resources, student attendance disputes, and faculty workload allocation.

roles.title: Academic Program Coordinator
roles.description: Supervises specific degree programs (e.g. B.Tech CSE), manages semester course timetables, credit overloads, and elective balancing.

roles.title: Faculty Advisor / Mentor
roles.description: Assigned faculty member mentoring a cohort of 20-30 students across 4 years, approving semester course registrations and tracking academic progress.

roles.title: Course Instructor / Professor
roles.description: Delivers classroom lectures, coordinates course content on LearnSphere LMS, conducts continuous internal assessments, and calculates CIE grades.

roles.title: Teaching Assistant (Graduate)
roles.description: Graduate M.Tech or Ph.D. student assisting course instructor with tutorial sessions, lab code reviews, and initial assignment evaluations.

roles.title: Technical Assistant (Lab Technician)
roles.description: Full-time technical staff maintaining physical hardware laboratories, instrument calibrations, component inventory, and machine safety.

roles.title: Research Assistant (Sponsored Projects)
roles.description: Postgraduate scholar employed under externally funded research grants conducting laboratory experiments and technical data analysis.

roles.title: Resident Assistant (Hostel Senior)
roles.description: Senior student resident assisting hostel wardens with floor attendance roll calls, facility maintenance logs, and junior student mentoring.

roles.title: Hostel Warden / Chief Warden
roles.description: Resident faculty or administrative officer managing hostel block operations, night curfews, gate pass approvals, and residential disciplinary conduct.

roles.title: Director of Placements and Corporate Relations
roles.description: Heads the Career Development Centre, leads corporate enterprise partnerships, establishes campus recruitment schedules, and enforces placement policy.

roles.title: University Chief Librarian
roles.description: Administers central library operations, academic subscriptions, digital repositories, institutional research archives, and plagiarism detection tools.

roles.title: Director of IT Infrastructure
roles.description: Supervises campus networking infrastructure, data center servers, cloud LMS/ERP systems, cybersecurity architecture, and user identity credentials.

roles.title: Chief Security Officer
roles.description: Directs 24/7 campus physical security personnel, gate turnstile access control, CCTV monitoring center, and campus emergency vigilance.

roles.title: Senior Chief Medical Officer
roles.description: Heads university health clinic, provides medical outpatient services, verifies sick leave condonations, and directs emergency medical response.

roles.title: Class Representative (Student)
roles.description: Elected student spokesperson for a classroom section communicating cohort feedback to course instructors, HODs, and student affairs.

cross_department_relationships.scenario: A resident student with pending hostel mess charges is unable to register for 5th semester courses in UniCampus ERP due to a financial hold flag.

participating_departments.role: Calculates outstanding mess bill dues and room damage charges.
Receives clearance payment on PayVarsity and updates central accounts ledger.

query_challenges.name: Polysemous Acronym Disambiguation
query_challenges.description: Students search using ambiguous 2-4 letter abbreviations that map to completely different entities (e.g. an academic course vs an administrative office).
query_challenges.student_behavior: Type bare acronyms or append vague suffixes without context (e.g. 'DSA timing', 'TA email', 'OD form', 'SEE schedule').

representative_queries.intent: Find Department of Student Affairs physical office hours
representative_queries.ambiguity: Could mean CS course teaching hours or student affairs administration.

representative_queries.intent: Find CSE201 Data Structures and Algorithms laboratory syllabus
representative_queries.ambiguity: Clear course intent, but naive search matches Department of Student Affairs annual report.

representative_queries.intent: Find assigned graduate Teaching Assistant for tutorial help
representative_queries.ambiguity: Could mean Technical Assistant for lab machinery or Travel Allowance policy in Finance.

representative_queries.intent: Check attendance On-Duty leave eligibility for attending a hackathon
representative_queries.ambiguity: Could match MBA Organizational Development course or Doctor of Optometry / medical.

representative_queries.intent: Download Semester End Examination schedule
representative_queries.ambiguity: Could match School of Electrical Engineering faculty notices.

query_challenges.naive_retrieval_failure: BM25 keyword search scores documents with highest term frequency, often surfacing the wrong entity (e.g. ranking a 50-page Department of Student Affairs handbook above a short CSE201 lab syllabus for 'DSA'). Standard dense embeddings collapse the acronym into an ambiguous vector centroid.
query_challenges.reformulation_strategy: Analyze accompanying query tokens, user role (UG Computer Science student vs general), active semester context, and expand acronym into canonical full form (e.g. rewrite 'DSA lab syllabus' -> 'CSE201 Data Structures and Algorithms laboratory practical syllabus manual Department of Computer Science').

query_challenges.name: Underspecified Procedural Queries
query_challenges.description: Short, fragmented procedural queries omitting the student's specific sub-situation or requirements.
query_challenges.student_behavior: Asking minimal keyword questions expecting the search engine to understand the unstated statutory goal.

representative_queries.intent: Obtain application steps, fees, and processing time for a bonafide student certificate
representative_queries.ambiguity: Doesn't state if it is for an education loan (requiring finance fee structure) or visa/bus pass.

representative_queries.intent: Steps to deactivate lost RFID badge and obtain duplicate smart card
representative_queries.ambiguity: Doesn't state if they want security gate entry permission, library replacement, or fine fee details.

representative_queries.intent: Find tuition fee due dates, online PayVarsity link, and installment options
representative_queries.ambiguity: Could be hostel fee, exam backlog fee, bus transport fee, or tuition fee.

representative_queries.intent: Procedure to switch hostel rooms on medical or personal preference grounds
representative_queries.ambiguity: Could mean lecture classroom allocation change for faculty or student hostel room transfer.

query_challenges.naive_retrieval_failure: Returns high-level administrative charters or generic lists containing the keyword 'bonafide' or 'fee' without presenting the exact actionable SOP or downloadable form.
query_challenges.reformulation_strategy: Expand the query to include procedural intent, canonical system names, and comprehensive forms (e.g. rewrite 'how to get bonafide' -> 'application procedure and required documents for bonafide student study certificate UniCampus ERP STU-FRM-001').

query_challenges.name: Informal / Distressed Failure Language Mismatch
query_challenges.description: Students searching during academic crises use colloquial, emotionally charged, or panicked phrases that never appear in formal university regulations.
query_challenges.student_behavior: Typing conversational or distress-driven queries when failing exams, facing detention, or missing tests.

representative_queries.raw: I failed a subject what now
representative_queries.intent: Find rules on backlog supplementary exams, summer semester, and re-evaluation
representative_queries.ambiguity: Matches zero formal terms since official documents use 'arrears', 'grade F', 'remedial examination'.

representative_queries.intent: Find supplementary examination schedule and eligibility rules
representative_queries.ambiguity: Informal phrasing for 'supplementary examination' or 'grade improvement evaluation'.

representative_queries.intent: Find attendance condonation rules, medical exceptions, and appeal procedure
representative_queries.ambiguity: Uses slang 'detained me' instead of 'ineligible for semester end examination due to attendance shortage'.

representative_queries.raw: caught with chit in exam hall
representative_queries.intent: Find disciplinary committee inquiry steps, penalties, and malpractice defense
representative_queries.ambiguity: Informal slang 'chit' vs official regulatory terminology 'unauthorized paper materials / examination malpractice Level 1-3'.

query_challenges.naive_retrieval_failure: Zero lexical overlap between student slang ('failed', 'chit', 'prof detained me') and formal statutory policy documents ('academic regulations', 'malpractice norms', 'condonation criteria'). Lexical engines return empty results or irrelevant disciplinary documents.
query_challenges.reformulation_strategy: Translate student distress language into formal regulatory taxonomy: map 'failed subject' -> 'backlog course supplementary examination fast-track summer term policy EXAM-GUI-002 POL-BACKLOG'; map 'caught with chit' -> 'examination malpractice inquiry committee procedure penalties EXAM-GUI-003'.
